THE 30-SECOND VERSION

Which blocker needs a manager’s attention today?

Rank by the need for intervention, with evidence behind every claim.

4brief categories
2core user groups
MockMVP data

Course project · mock-data MVP. Research scope and measurement limits are explained below.

01 / PROBLEM

The cost is late discovery

Managers reconstruct team status by moving between chat, issues, code reviews and email. The deeper problem is that blockers may remain invisible until a standup or one-to-one, after time has already been lost.

02 / CONTRIBUTION

What I worked on

I defined the problem, manager and team-member personas, user stories, priorities, MVP scope and system components. The supporting work includes a PRD, UI design, workflow diagrams and a demonstration video.

03 / EVIDENCE

Make the assumptions visible

The PRD separates contextual research from unvalidated assumptions. Whether an LLM can identify real blockers accurately, whether managers act on the brief, and whether team members trust the system all require real-team validation.

04 / DECISION

An intervention brief, not an activity feed

The feed should rank work by its need for attention and explain that ranking. A busy thread is not automatically a blocker. Every claim should link back to its evidence so the manager can understand and challenge it.

05 / SOLUTION

One brief, then an action

The design groups information into blocked work, items needing attention, top work and yesterday’s changes. Managers can inspect the evidence and assign, complete or snooze an item. Team members have a transparency view and a way to dispute an incorrect inference.

06 / TRADEOFFS

Visibility without surveillance

The MVP uses mock data; real Slack, issue-tracker and GitHub ingestion are outside its implemented scope. Employee performance analytics are excluded. Transparency and dispute handling are part of the product design rather than a later policy layer.

07 / MEASUREMENT

Measure response, not reading

The proposed north star is median time to blocker acknowledgement, with a target below four hours. Dismissal rate is a guardrail. These are PRD targets and do not describe measured production performance.

08 / LEARNING

Prove the signal before adding integrations

The next useful test is to compare the brief with managers’ actual intervention decisions and examine false positives. More connected data will not rescue a ranking that people cannot trust.
